en: The Gaṇḍī-stava composed by Ācārya Āryadeva:
O gods down to the limits of the netherworld (Pātāla), along with men, Garuḍas, Daityas, Gandharvas, and Yakṣas!

The Siddhas, Vidyādharas, and others, along with all the noble Nāgas dwelling on the shores of the ocean, have gathered here with hearts agitated by the sound of the Gaṇḍī; they sit upon these seats, serene and steadfast, eager to hear [the teaching] of this virtuous one, the kinsman of the three worlds, who possesses a multitude of stainless qualities. (1)
Oho! The city resounded with the playful waving of chowries, shimmering with the elaborate display of girdles, and tinkling with the sounds of golden bells;
it echoed with the cries of swans and was graced by women whose limbs were as dark as the petals of fresh blue lotuses in their youth.
Salutation to that Buddha, whose mind never underwent any transformation.

May there be well-being for those who possess faith in the Blessed One, the Sugata who is engaged in the conquest of Māra; for those who have immediately become clear-minded toward the work of the Son of the Sugata; and for those whose devotion lies in this world in the auspicious deeds of the Teacher, the Lion of the Śākyas, after he has struck the gong.
Having established her in the inner apartments, all those of well-disciplined minds come to listen.

I bow to the Buddha, Lord of the three worlds, saluted by gods and men; who has reached the further shore of saṃsāra, who is steadfast and profound, a treasury of all virtues, consecrated in the sovereignty of Dharma;
the one who brings an end to the enemy of craving, who removes the defilement of the Kali age, and who brings an end to desire and greed.
I bow to that Lion of the Śākyas; with my head bowed in prostration, I pay homage to him at all times. || 4 ||
Ṛmpaṃ ṛmpaṃ ṛṛmpaṃ, ṭama ṭama ṭaṭamaṃ, tundatundaṃ tutundaṃ, saṃ saṃ saṃ saṃ saṃ saṃ saṃ, samasamamasamaṃ, durma durma drudurmam;
nāgirnāgirnanāgistakhitakhitakhitastatyajurye raṇe vai.
By whom, by whom, and by whom else in this world is the Dharma-gong proclaimed as the remover of fear? (5)
"Make ready, make ready the armor of meditation upon the Blessed One!
Before the irresistible Lord of Death devours him who is immersed in it," so spoke the multitude of people, and by this they were awakened, O community of monks.
Having destroyed the faction of evil, they are free from all defects without exception.
He upon whose rising the entire triple world emerges, and upon whose setting it goes to its end;
he by whom, through the spreading rays of his hands of wisdom, the hand [of liberation] is extended;
he who possesses the orb of the stainless True Dharma, who is endowed with the ten powers, and who brings an end to the night of saṃsāra—[to him, the Buddha, I bow].
May the Buddha, the sun among sages and kinsman of all beings, protect the hosts of gods. || 7 ||
By him whose mind—fickle as a lordly elephant—was conquered by the syllables of wisdom rather than by goads;
by whom the dense veil of the darkness of passion was destroyed by the fire of knowledge rather than by physical fire;
and by whom the host of Māra was shattered by one of tranquil intellect through the weapons of patience rather than by martial arms.
I pay homage to that awakened Buddha, the Sage, who is skilled at destroying the suffering of those who bow before him. || 8 ||
Swiftly shattering the army of the heretics, established in the highest heaven (Nākaniṣṭha), descending into the world with abundant splendors that terrify with their brilliance,
Lakṣmī stands upon a great golden lion-throne situated at the base of the netherworld (Pātāla).
May the One of Ten Powers, who has displayed his miraculous transformations, himself grant you the light of song.

That king, having dispelled the fierce heat of summer with his beautiful breath purified by mantras, easily breaks apart that very same massive rock— which the other king had hurled at his big toe with great stones and the like—
while being terrified by it.
The perfected ones (siddhas) bowed to the world; may that all-seeing Blessed One grant us prosperity. 10.
The forms of Māra and his hosts— terrifying at the time of universal dissolution, with girdles bound and fastened,
holding various sharp-pointed weapons in their hands, with faces like elephants and horses, and roaring lion-like roars—
were shattered by him who led [them] to Buddhahood; and the assemblies of monks were beheld by her whose eyes are like the petals of the blue water-lily.
Listen to the beloved Dharma, which is exceedingly skillful at destroying the misdeeds of the heretics. || 11 ||

The mind of that woman whose heart was not swiftly agitated by the graceful, darting side-glances of her lover’s tremulous eyes, nor by the well-pressed weight of her jar-like breasts adorned with strings of pearls—
for her this gong of Dharma rings out its sweet, melodious sound for the assembly of monks.
Listen to that beloved Dharma of his, which causes supreme terror to the heretics. || 12 ||

He who is glorious, with a joyful mind at the wheel of Dharma, wearing the unique crown-jewel of the Dharma-treasure; who, seated upon a lion-throne, resembling a mountain of gold, utters the roar of the Dharma with a full body and a blossoming face, pouring forth the jewels of the Dharma.
This drum of Dharma of his resounds constantly; listen to it, O followers of the Jina! (13)
"Ma-mā-mā! Mīya-kaṇṭhaiḥ! Ḍima-ḍima-ga-gatā! Gā-ga-gāgaiḥ galantaiḥ!

Nā-nā-nā! No-pa-nī-tam! Nanu nanu nanu mā! Dhurya-mādhurya-kāntaiḥ!"—by these songs of the women of Kāma, whose voices were so lovely in their sweetness and power, his mind was not moved, nor did he find peace.
For that banner of Dharma, this fierce drum resounds with the sharp sound of a drum.
Are these the forest-dwellers of the *saṃvarta* fire, emitting long and furious roars?
Or is it the destruction of the *nirvāṭa* wind? Or perhaps the *hūṃ*-utterance of the Blessed One Vajrapāṇi?
All of this is indeed the inner activity of the people’s minds as they proceed to perceive the teachings.
This is that very sound of the Gāṇḍīva bow, which causes terror to the thirty gods, belonging to the Buddha whose form is sublime.

O Sole Friend of the Universe, whose feet are bowed by the crest-jewels of the lords of gods, you have summoned the lords of mountains— whose forms are like fierce lions with mangled claws and mouths, who are hosts of Māras of vital energy, and who possess manifest clusters of jewels in the jewel-lamp of the netherworld (Pātāla).
This drum of the Lion of the Śākyas, which bestows auspiciousness, resounds as it is struck by the ascetics. 16.
O Lord Kīrtinātha, let Cupid be subdued; for the truth regarding You, the enemy of Māra, is sung before those who uplift the wretched and the helpless:
*khinda khinda khikhinda khuda khuda sukhadaṃ dattake dattutundaṃ*.
Tunda, Tunda, Tutunda—[they were addressed] by the Siddhas, Gandharvas, and Nāgas with the resonant sounds of drums. || 17 ||
By Māras of various kinds— with hundreds of distorted faces, many mouths, blazing and terrifying, with loud, boisterous laughter, devouring raw flesh, roaring lion-like roars;
appearing as the very form of Time, manifold, causing dense fear, and terrifying from every side—
May he whose mind is constantly pervaded by [the thought of Māra] not for even a moment—may that destroyer of Māra protect you all. || 18 ||
May the king rule a realm free of thorns; may the earth be filled with all kinds of crops; may the clouds rain in due season; may all people be free from calamity;
and may there be the complete pacification of all obstacles for all men in their religious practice and the fulfillment of their actions.
May the noble Saṅgha, free from passion, become filled with happiness through the state of mutual affection. || 19 ||
The Teacher’s jewel of the True Dharma, impelling the excellent sons of the Sugata, purifies those deluded by passion and hatred who have entered upon uneven paths; it resounds as it conquers,
delivering sentient beings through hundreds of arrows of tranquility, possessing manifest meaning.
Bringing peace to the people, he captivates the Teacher with various excellent sounds. || 20 ||
Scattering the noble women, roaring with fierce and loud laughter amidst a multitude of hosts,
leaping, quivering, and bestowing a grace as lovely as a blazing crest of fire; wandering about with intense passion and speaking bold words, he exercises sovereignty over the realm of desire.
I pay homage to that Buddha-hero, the truly valiant one, worthy of veneration, who removes all fear. 21.

When the lotus of the thumb is perfected, [the practitioner] instantly [visualizes the deity] in the heart, as well as in the throat and near the throat, accompanied by the sounds of *ḍhakkā* drums, rhythmic clapping, and the sharp, clear resonance of *paṭaha* drums, along with the blaring blasts of conchs;
and those who have uttered "Hā! Hā! Huṃ! Hūṃ! with sudden, rattling, and terrifying roars of approval.
Salutations to him whose mind is not base, and who has conquered the best of the gods. || 22 ||
She, who is praised by great beings— by various lords of serpents and yakṣas with hundreds of trembling hymns, and by divine musical sounds clear and resonant with specific utterances;
she who is the Maheśvarī-yāna in the Sāṃkhya system, the supreme teacher of the asuras...
...the Māras begin their assault, yet she, held in the palms of her hands, cries out for peace from the enemies of the gods. || 23 ||
Having given away all his possessions, hundreds of sacrifices made of gold, or even his kingdom, his son, his wife, his own body, his head, or a thousand eyes—
since he would have exhausted [his merit] even after hundreds of years by such expenditures.
Perfect enlightenment is supreme; may that Sugata bring peace to virtuous people. || 24 ||

The minds of those wise ones were not shaken in the slightest by the followers of Māra— those who, through various forms, misshapen sights, and transformations, repeatedly seek to devour with ashes and with the blazing bonds of light produced by the obstruction of consciousness within women.
Or, through dances for the Sugata, the Conqueror of Māra, the gong resounds wondrously. || 25 ||

Hearing whose sound, which brings delight to the ears, the hungry ghosts (pretas) such as Bhūmimukha and others— who possess massive bodies and are overwhelmed by hunger and thirst— attain complete satisfaction on all sides;
and who is heard with clarity by gods and humans of noble form who listen with perfect devotion.
May that beautiful and honored gong protect the universe—[the gong] of him who possesses the power of the ten strengths. 26.

By him, the army of Māra— accompanied by warriors and resounding with the cries of various musical instruments, lordly elephants, horses, buffaloes, tigers, and the like, and uplifted with flickering spears, excellent arrows, lances, clubs, discuses, and other weapons— was shattered in an instant.
May this *gaṇḍikā* protect the world of that Blessed One, the treasury of compassion. (27)

Those whose minds are agitated by the Dharma, whose methods are destroyed by the power of passion, and who are always sinful—let the virtuous be restrained in generosity, morality, patience, and compassionate study.
Thus, with very sweet sounds, she awakens all sentient beings; she is pure.
Therefore, by our meritorious words, may the entire ghaṇṭā of the Buddha-hero resound throughout the three worlds. 28.

Listening attentively, through the practice of the arrows of tranquility, Ānandavajrī did not hear even the sound of the gods led by Indra, nor the sounds of the cries of distress from the lords of the sages who had become her captives— sounds produced by the intensity of their gestures and the eloquence of their proclamations— just as the high tide does not heed the roar of the ocean king.
The gong, through the resonance following the sequence of blows from its staff, vibrates like a kettledrum. || 29 ||
Huṃkārī, the lotus-born, the beloved of the conqueror of Tripura, the trident-wielder, Viṣṇu, the wielder of the thunderbolt, the lord of the gods who destroys the asuras, the wielder of the discus—
whatever others there may be who praise you with their own voices in a state of agitation, what remains [unattained] for them?
All have approached with humility at the base of his feet; I praise him with songs of mantra. || 30 ||
Causing the ignorant to wander through the three worlds while leading the lords who are omniscient together with the feet of the Munis;
terrifying all the Māras by various other means that cause manifold fears;
driving away all evils; and awakening the wise from their thoughts of delight in sense-objects.
In this world, the gong of the Lion of the Śākyas proclaims those whose awakening is obstructed by loud noises. (31)

Having given his own body to a tigress, he who has attained Buddhahood— won through a mass of merit and a multitude of hundreds of virtues— he whose evil is obstructed, who seeks to intoxicate the god of love,
who is the peerless Teacher, and who shatters the fear of existence while breaking the intent of sin; [to him I bow].
This is indeed that wonderful gong of the Blessed One, the Lion of the Śākyas, which resounds.
May that Lord Śākyasiṃha, the King of Sages and the most excellent of Jinas, who was born from the womb of Queen Māyā and who,
amidst a multitude of preeminent sages at the foot of the world-tree,
was bathed by the lords of gods, Brahmā, Rudra, asuras, humans, and celestial beings— may he [grant us grace].
I worship that Lord of Sages, whose body is ground by the rays of the moon, with jewels of devotion. 33.

Even by Māras of various kinds—with swords, axes, bows, and arrows in their hands; with blazing, terrifying faces, wicked fangs, and the heads of elephants, serpents, lions, and dogs—his feet were not The entire world will surely go [to that state], free from fear; therefore, the gaṇḍī-bell should be sounded for them.
The *Śrīgaṇḍīstava* is completed.
This work is by the venerable master Āryadeva.
